To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) there is a PCS algorithm for which the rejection rate depends only on Hanneke’s disagreement coefficient, (ii) the disagreement coefficient can be exponentially small, and (iii) this implies an exponential speedup in active learning.

(a) the existence of fast PCS learning algorithms is equivalent to an exponentially faster disagreement based active learning algorithm (ActiveiLESS) and (b) the existence of PCS learning algorithms is intimately tied to the disagreement coefficient.

(1) the disagreement coefficient is a fundamental quantity in agnostic active learning; (2) it is a sufficient condition for the existence of PCS classifiers with a fast rejection rate; (3) it is also a sufficient condition for an exponential speedup in the performance of disagreement-based active learners; and (4) in the realizable setting, it is also a necessary condition.
